title: plugin-v6: bump crate versions to 11.0.0
body:
Once all the plugin-v6-related PRs are merged (see https://github.com/qemu-rs/qemu-rs/pull/42, https://github.com/qemu-rs/qemu-rs/pull/50, https://github.com/qemu-rs/qemu-rs/pull/51), qemu-rs supports all the QEMU v11.0.0-supported plugin APIs. We can therefore bump the version accordingly.

Closes #43.

title: plugin-v6: add syscall filter API functions
body:
The syscall filter API allows to set a syscall's return value and skip actually executing it. This functionality was introduced in QEMU 11.0 in the patchset here:
https://lore.kernel.org/qemu-devel/20260129013134.3956938-1-pierrick.bouvier@linaro.org/

This is part of the changes mentioned in #43.

title: plugin-v6: add qemu_plugin_set_pc API
body:
Control-flow diversion via writing the PC does not work via the original register write API, as this has no direct effect on the execution. Upstream QEMU introduced a qemu_plugin_set_pc API in version 11.0 for this purpose (see
https://lore.kernel.org/qemu-devel/20260305-setpc-v5-v7-0-4c3adba52403@epfl.ch/).

I contemplated adding a special case in the `RegisterDescriptor::write` method, but that seemed brittle and is not really mirroring upstream. For the sake of simplicity, I therefore think that exposing this API directly as I do in this PR makes more sense. Opinions welcome, however!

This is part of the changes mentioned in #43.

title: Rust support upstream
MSRV needs to be bumped to at least 1.89
body: In `qemu-plugin` we use `std::fs::TryLockError`, which was stabilized in Rust 1.89. We therefore need to bump the MSRV to that. Usually this would also mean a major version bump and there _are_ some reasons why we may want to do that in the near future. But the builds for Rust 1.88 are already broken for the last release so the "correct" path forward is not obvious imo.

title: Replace PluginU64 alias with struct and add Scoreboard fn for creating it
body: Closes #46.

title: PluginU64 construction for a Scoreboard
body:
At least as far as I can tell there is currently no way to construct a `PluginU64` for entries in a `scoreboard::Scoreboard`. `PluginU64::score` is a `*mut qemu_plugin_scoreboard` which is currently not accessible but wrapped in a `scoreboard::Scoreboard`.

You can build a scoreboard by hand, but that's not really what we want here. At the same time, getting the lifetime constraints right is probably messy.

title: High-level plugin api for exec_inline
body:
`qemu-plugin` currently does not feature high-level API for registering inline operations for instruction or TB execution. The former (instruction execution) is not exposed at all.

We probably want:
- [ ] one free fn `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_insn_exec_inline_per_vcpu` (like the existing `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_tb_exec_inline_per_vcpu`).
- [ ] one `translation_block::TranslationBlock` fn `register_execute_inline`
- [ ] one `instruction::Instruction` fn `register_execute_inline`

title: mem: fix memory corruption when reading guest vaddr
body:
While testing my plugin I was experiencing frequent hangs with call stacks like:

```
(lldb) bt
* thread #11, stop reason = EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=2, address=0x1e6a3720c)
  * frame #0: 0x0000000188afe050 libsystem_platform.dylib`__bzero + 32
    frame #1: 0x0000000103807fac libglib-2.0.0.dylib`g_array_set_size + 136
    frame #2: 0x0000000103809c00 libglib-2.0.0.dylib`g_byte_array_set_size + 20
    frame #3: 0x00000001024c7f8c xemu`qemu_plugin_read_memory_vaddr(addr=9582356, data=0x000000016e31e598, len=<unavailable>) at api.c:571:5 [opt]
    frame #4: 0x000000011e1d44ec libsplinter_cell_qemu_plugin.dylib`qemu_plugin::memory::qemu_plugin_read_memory_vaddr::h9ff5b36bf22ea5d5(addr=9582356, buf=(data_ptr = "", length = 4)) at mod.rs:214:9
    frame #5: 0x000000011e1ca9b0 libsplinter_cell_qemu_plugin.dylib`_$LT$splinter_cell_qemu_plugin..SplinterCellDumper$u20$as$u20$qemu_plugin..plugin..HasCallbacks$GT$::on_translation_block_translate::_$u7b$$u7b$closure$u7d$$u7d$::_$u7b$$u7b$closure$u7d$$u7d$::he7f008294245bb95(vcpu=0) at lib.rs:118:25
    frame #6: 0x000000011e1c7d74 libsplinter_cell_qemu_plugin.dylib`_$LT$alloc..boxed..Box$LT$F$C$A$GT$$u20$as$u20$core..ops..function..FnMut$LT$Args$GT$$GT$::call_mut::h94c7af4678ae8d40(self=0x0000000bdb697fa0, args=(__0 = 0)) at boxed.rs:1992:9
```

Or occasionally I'd `SIGSEGV`.

While walking through this code, I noticed that `GByteArray` gets cast to a `GRealArray` which has a _much bigger_ size than `GByteArray`: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/blob/91524a98c54e57f1b609d95131480bdd15ebb43f/glib/garray.c#L768

The `GByteArray` is defined as a smaller size as not to reveal internal details of `GRealArray`. This means that the current implementation will trigger an out-of-bounds read/write when attempting to set the array size.

The correct way of interfacing with these APIs is to have glib construct the `GByteArray`, then pass that pointer to these APIs.

With this patch my plugin now works as expected.

Note: a similar bug exists in `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` but I have not yet tested an equivalent fix for that.

title: Add cdylib options that can replace unix-weak-link feature
body:
Have the qemu-plugin-sys crate's build script set link options that will allow downstream cdylibs to build without requiring the `unix-weak-link` feature.

This has a few benefits:
1. Works on macOS.
2. Doesn't use the `linkage` feature so a nightly complier isn't needed.
3. Won't accidentally use one of the weakly-linked symbols if there's a typo (although this could also be solved by putting `unimplemented!()` or `panic!()` into the weakly-linked versions).

Fixes: https://github.com/novafacing/qemu-rs/issues/27

title: Possibly remove `unix-weak-link` feature
body:
I was testing `qemu-plugin` on macOS (aarch64-apple-darwin) and having some trouble getting the examples running.  The issue turned out to be with the `unix-weak-link` feature that the examples enable.  (Debug builds would link, but release builds would fail with lots of undefined symbols.  Even then, the debug build wouldn't actually execute the plugin code when loaded via `qemu-system-x86_64 -plugin target/debug/*.dylib`.)

As I was debugging/thinking about that issue, I started to believe that using weak linking as done with that feature in "qemu-plugin/src/unix_weak_link/mod.rs" is probably not the "right" way to prevent the cdylib builds from failing due to undefined symbols.  On one hand it's not portable (as seen with the macOS issues), and on the other it can accidentally hide errors (a symbol that isn't actually in qemu, for example due to a typo, will silently use the weakly-linked copy).

I think the more standard solution is to tell the linker to allow undefined symbols in the cdylib.  That would allow the  `unix-weak-link` feature and its `unix_weak_link` module to be deleted altogether and any actually-missing symbols would cause `dlopen()` to fail when qemu tries to load the plugin (instead of silently using the weakly-linked copy's dummy implementation).

This can be done with the following linker options in ".cargo/config.toml":
```toml
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")']
rustflags = ["-Clink-arg=-undefined", "-Clink-arg=dynamic_lookup"]

[target.'cfg(all(target_family = "unix", not(target_os = "macos")))']
rustflags = ["-C", "link-args=-Wl,-z,undefs"]
```

title: qemu_plugin_get_registers() segfaults when linked along with Unicorn
body:
Definitely one of the weirder bugs I've come across.

When linking `qemu-plugin` and `unicorn_engine` together, `g_array_free` appears to get merged by the linker. However, it appears their implementations are slightly different, causing the `g_array_free` call from within `sys::qemu_plugin_get_registers()` to segfault.

Building `unicorn_engine` with `features = ["dynamic_linkage"]` works but, of course, requires that you have the `.so.2` on hand somewhere in the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, which is unideal.

I don't even know what could be done to 'fix' this. I'm pretty certain `qemu_plugin_get_registers()` is just the first place this would pop up, so e.g. allowing the array to leak given some option wouldn't really solve the real problem.

I've never seen a linker merge two very obviously different functions from different libraries in such a catastrophic way before, but here we are.

```
#1  0x00007ffffa030bb5 in array_free (array=0xa9cd160, flags=(FREE_SEGMENT | PRESERVE_WRAPPER))
    at /home/anonymous/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/unicorn-engine-2.0.1/glib_compat/garray.c:352
#2  0x00007ffffa030c84 in g_array_free (farray=0xa9cd160, free_segment=1)
    at /home/anonymous/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/unicorn-engine-2.0.1/glib_compat/garray.c:338
#3  0x00007ffffa02af8b in qemu_plugin::qemu_plugin_get_registers () at src/lib.rs:1698
#4  0x00007ffff9fce3da in seminal_qemu::{impl#1}::on_vcpu_init (self=0x9af6340, 
    _id=16409229355086296901, vcpu_id=0) at seminal-qemu/src/lib.rs:142
#5  0x00007ffffa022164 in qemu_plugin::plugin::handle_qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_init_cb (
    id=16409229355086296901, vcpu_id=0) at src/plugin/mod.rs:2
```

Was shocked to see the qemu plugin code jumping into the unicorn side of things. Just wanted to raise the issue with you! Almost definitely a side effect of Unicorn being built from QEMU sources, which itself is a bit unfortunate.

title: Fix segfaults inside g_free on windows
body:
This should fix #13.

calling `libc::free` actually doesn't always work, because there are multiple heaps, and we're trying to free it from the wrong one.

Instead, we find the g_free export from libglib-2.0, and invoke that.

Added the `libloading` crate to help with this, and also rewrote the `delaylink_hook` to use the functions there, rather than directly calling the windows API.

title: suggestions to tidy up the windows linking code.
body:
https://github.com/novafacing/qemu-rs/blob/2d1c40de8a5731227e87249ca0f0dc78e25bb5a9/qemu-plugin/src/win_link_hook/mod.rs#L51

Note that the "qemu.exe"  here is not the name of the calling executable, but rather the name of the delay-linked DLL that is created in https://github.com/novafacing/qemu-rs/blob/2d1c40de8a5731227e87249ca0f0dc78e25bb5a9/qemu-plugin-sys/build.rs#L22-L32. I used `qemu.exe` because there was some chatter on the qemu-devel mailing list about moving (eventually) to a single-executable based approach, at which point much of this machinery would be unnecessary.

`qemu-system-arm.exe` loads `plugin.dll`, then `plugin.dll` loads `qemu.exe`. The win_link_hook module intercepts the failure to load `qemu.exe`, and returns a reference to the top-level executable (regardless of how it is named).

So, a few comments:
* There is an unfinished safety justification on line 46: https://github.com/novafacing/qemu-rs/blob/2d1c40de8a5731227e87249ca0f0dc78e25bb5a9/qemu-plugin/src/win_link_hook/mod.rs#L46-L47
* Because you're hooking failure rather than notification now, if there happens to be a "qemu.exe" on the DLL load path, then the plugin will load that instead of getting a reference to the calling binary. It's a weird situation, and I'm not sure which behaviour is preferable.
* as above, the check on line 51 is OK as is, but also it was fine before, too. Now, if the plugin happens to also link to other `qemu*` DLLs and they fail to load, then we will reroute to the calling executable. This might surprise the user.
* unfinished comment on line 43.

title: support for windows plugins
body:
This is intended to fix #3.

Here's my first (mostly successful) go at this. I'll add explanatory comments into the changes, but at a high level:

* `generate_bindings.rs` now (on windows) also creates `qemu_plugin_api.def`
* the (new) `build.rs` script for `qemu-plugin-sys` (on windows) makes the appropriate delay link .lib file from the .def. This only works in gnu-style toolchains, not -msvc style.
* I've dropped in the delay link hook to `qemu-plugin`. It works without further config on the plugins side.
* `g_free` is a problem - windows doesn't expose functions unless asked to, so we don't have an (easy) way of getting access to `g_free`. For now I've implemented it as a no-op, and so we leak memory whenever it's used.

The tiny example compiles and runs on my windows machine, as does my internal more complex plugin. `tracer` doesn't compile because it uses `memfd`, which doesn't work on windows.

Limitations:

* `-gnu` only, because I'm using dlltool. there may be a way to get this to work on `-msvc`, but I've not looked into it.
* `g_free` leaks

title: Windows support for plugins
body:
The qemu-plugin API is much nicer than Cannonball, thanks for that.

Currently, compiling `examples/tiny` on windows (in an msys environment) fails with linker errors:

```
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.3nlexlhtiloges53.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_bool_parse referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin7install5Value3new17hb19820019c468133E
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_tb_n_insns referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin16TranslationBlock4size17h6288dd76d0ce99c8E
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_tb_vaddr referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin16TranslationBlock5vaddr17hae96755f780c793bE
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_tb_get_insn referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin16TranslationBlock11instruction17h95c07ba18e8437e9E
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_insn_data referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin11Instruction4data17h2f87c2c1751b7776E
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_insn_size referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin11Instruction4size17h2e6d0fb9fd0bdbf3E
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_insn_vaddr referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin11Instruction5vaddr17h8f7411fc30897e77E
          libqemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.rlib(qemu_plugin-9b366b86ee3df11c.2vy382h4jhrt5nnw.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol qemu_plugin_insn_haddr referenced in function _ZN11qemu_plugin11Instruction5haddr17h755f98d4c9ff9ddcE
          ....many more like it....
```

...this is because windows doesn't let you have unresolved references in a DLL (see [notes where I worked on this in base here](https://www.mail-archive.com/qemu-devel@nongnu.org/msg1003961.html)).

To get windows support, we will need:

* A way to acquire or build a `qemu_plugin_api.lib` to help produce the delay-loaded dll, and link from build.rs
  * This is made during qemu building, but it seems expensive to build all of qemu just to be able to make a plugin for it.
  * It can be made from the file [`qemu_plugins.symbols`, as shown in the build.rs snippet here](https://gist.github.com/tocklime/bd91136593353e7cf2907504c3bb5f85#file-build-rs)
* A way to hook into the `__pfnDliFailureHook2` symbol. I have [this working locally](https://gist.github.com/tocklime/bd91136593353e7cf2907504c3bb5f85#file-win_link_hook-rs).

The hook should just work. The build.rs snippet there will need work though - I'm not sure how to get the input file `qemu_plugin_api.def`, and also not sure how to ensure `dlltool` is lying around for use. Given qemu only builds in msys on Windows, it seems reasonable to expect an msys environment/rust target for this.

Anyway, I'm just trying to collate my notes here for comment. Happy to assemble a PR if we can work work out the details.
